title: Stop the payments client from giving up on a throttled request

blocks.text: The payments client sends each request through `RetryPolicy`, which looks at the HTTP status of every response and decides what to do next. The on-call log from last week has two complaints: requests that the provider throttled were dropped instead of retried, and a misbehaving proxy that answered with status `600` kept the client retrying.
The policy the team agreed on:

`attempts(...)` already drives a request from these decisions. Write `decide(int status)` in `src/main/java/practice/RetryPolicy.java` so that it follows the table for every `int`. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: a success, a client error, a server error and a redirect each get the action the policy lists
a request is retried after server errors and stops at the first response that ends it
429 and 503 are retried later, although they also lie inside the 4xx and 5xx ranges
200, 299, 400, 499, 500 and 599 get the action of their class
a status above 599, below 200 or negative is unexpected, not retried

origin.section: An else-if Chain Runs the First Branch That Holds, So the Order Is the Specification

concepts: The comparison at each boundary of a range decides which branch the boundary value takes.
An else-if chain runs only the first branch whose condition holds, so a special case inside a range must come before the range.
